nodes.description: More biologically active erythropoietin reaching the marrow than the red cell mass warrants. The two variant classes differ in how this presents in the laboratory: the exon 2 route was described as excess production, while in the noncoding families circulating concentrations stay inside the reference interval and the excess is one of activity rather than amount. What is raised is the hormone's own action: in the noncoding families the protein sequence is unchanged, and erythropoietin purified from patient plasma signals more strongly through its receptor than wild-type hormone, which is a quantitative increase in an otherwise normal activity rather than a new one.

nodes.description: Erythropoietin receptor signaling in marrow erythroid progenitors is driven above its normal set point. No progenitor culture from an EPO-variant patient has been reported, so the cell type here is the one erythropoietin is known to act on rather than one assayed in these families.

The sentinel allele. A single G deletion in exon 2 that truncates the erythropoietin signal peptide and frameshifts the normally noncoding intron 1 transcript into the erythropoietin coding frame.

The tg6 line carries a human EPO transgene expressed independently of oxygen tension, so erythropoietin drive is permanently uncoupled from the hypoxia signal that normally gates it. That is the same uncoupling the EPO variants produce in patients, which is why the model is informative here; the model reaches it by a transgene rather than by an EPO allele, and at a far higher hematocrit than patients carry. Beyond the red cell mass the model also develops hepatic, renal, neuronal and muscular degeneration, a reduced lifespan, endothelial activation with reduced brain vessel density, and near-loss of the endothelial glycocalyx. None of those is a reported feature of human ECYT5 and none is curated as a phenotype of this disease; see the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion.
